'''''Juncus subulatus''''', called the '''Somerset rush''', is a species of flowering plant in the genus ''[[Juncus]]'', with a Mediterranean, Middle Eastern and Central Asian distribution, and introduced to Great Britain.<ref name="443542-1" >{{cite web |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:443542-1 |title=''Juncus subulatus'' Forssk. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2017 |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=23 February 2021 }}</ref><ref name = "25_botanists" >{{cite web |url=https://www.thewildflowersociety.com/wfs_reports/1998/1998_somerset_2_august_report.htm |title=1998 Somerset 2 August One Day Meeting |last=Green |first=Ian |date=2 August 1998 |website=thewildflowersociety.com |publisher=The Wild Flower Society |access-date=23 February 2021 }}</ref> It typically grows in salt marshes.<ref name="1_of_708_Google_Scholar_Hits" >{{cite journal |last1= Espinar|first1= J. L.|last2= Thompson|first2= K.|last3= Garcia|first3= L. V.|date=1 October 2005 |title=Timing of seed dispersal generates a bimodal seed bank depth distribution |journal=American Journal of Botany |volume=92 |issue=10 |pages=1759–1763 |doi=10.3732/ajb.92.10.1759 |pmid= 21646093|doi-access=free |hdl=10261/35075 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>
